```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
knitr::knit_hooks$set(inline = function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) x <- format(x, big.mark = ",")
  paste(x, collapse = ", ")
})
```

The MetaMorpheus tool output has two peptide sequence columns:
`Full Sequence`, which includes the modifications, and `Base Sequence`, which
does not. MSstats needs the sequence with the modifications, since otherwise
the modified and unmodified forms of a peptide are merged into one feature. In
the rows that a language model is shown, the two columns are often the same,
since most peptides carry no modification. This vignette shows the two
columns, the example rows where they look the same, and what the choice does
to the differential abundance analysis. The conversion specification and the
results of the analysis were obtained once and saved, so the vignette runs
without a language model or the full tool output.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(MSstatsConvertLLM)
library(data.table)
```

# The tool output

We use the MetaMorpheus output of the Solivais2024 benchmark, in which
*E. coli* proteins are spiked in different amounts into a constant human
background. We distribute the rows of the tool output that the model was
shown. The benchmark of the manuscript normalized the column names before
showing them to the model, replacing spaces and other characters by dots, and
the conversion specification uses these names. In these rows, the base and the
full sequence are the same.

```{r tool-output}
case <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "metamorpheus_case_study.rds",
                            package = "MSstatsConvertLLM"))
tool_output <- normalize_headers(case$tool_output)
tool_output[, .(Base.Sequence, Full.Sequence, Precursor.Charge, Peak.intensity)]
all(tool_output$Base.Sequence == tool_output$Full.Sequence)
```

# Inferring the conversion specification

`infer_specification()` sends the model the column names and the first
`r formals(infer_specification)$n_preview` rows of the tool output. We obtained
the saved conversion specification with the call below, using llama3.1-8b and
the lean prompt, in the benchmark of the manuscript.

```{r infer-live, eval = FALSE}
specification <- infer_specification(tool_output, "llama3.1-8b", "lean",
                                     acquisition = "DDA")
```

Here, we read the saved conversion specification instead.

```{r infer-saved}
specification <- case$specification
as.data.frame(specification$mappings)[, c("field", "from", "confidence")]
```

# Checking the peptide sequence

The model chose `Base.Sequence`, the sequence without the modifications. The
example rows give no reason to prefer either column, since the two are the
same there. They differ on modified peptides. The tool output reports the
peptide below with and without the oxidation of a methionine, in the same run,
at the same charge and in the same protein group.

```{r peptide-sequences}
peptide_sequences <- normalize_headers(case$peptide_sequences)
peptide_sequences[, .(Base.Sequence, Full.Sequence, Precursor.Charge,
                      Peak.intensity)]
```

Read by the full sequence, the two rows are two peptides. Read by the base
sequence, they are one, and the LLM-based converter takes them as two
measurements of one feature and keeps the larger.

```{r count-peptide-sequences}
c(full = uniqueN(peptide_sequences$Full.Sequence),
  base = uniqueN(peptide_sequences$Base.Sequence))
```

The hand-written converter, `MetamorpheusToMSstatsFormat()`, reads
`Full Sequence`, which `GOLD_STANDARD` lists for the peptide sequence.

```{r gold-standard}
GOLD_STANDARD$metamorpheus$PeptideSequence
```

# Differential abundance results

We converted the full tool output with the hand-written converter, which
reads `Full Sequence`, and with the LLM-based converter and the model's
conversion specification, which reads `Base Sequence`. We then analyzed both
with MSstats, as below. The script `compare_solivais.R` in the GitHub
repository of the package runs these steps, after keeping the peaks of single
human or *E. coli* protein groups.

```{r analysis-live, eval = FALSE}
peaks <- fread("QuantifiedPeaks.tsv")
annotation <- fread("annotation.csv")

converted <- list(
  hand = MSstatsConvert::MetamorpheusToMSstatsFormat(peaks,
                                                     annotation = annotation),
  llm  = LLMtoMSstatsFormat(normalize_headers(peaks), annotation = annotation,
                            specification = specification))
processed <- lapply(converted, MSstats::dataProcess,
                    normalization = "equalizeMedians")
# contrast: each condition against condition A
compared <- lapply(processed, function(p) MSstats::groupComparison(contrast, p))
```

Here, we read the saved results instead. They have one row per protein and
comparison. For each converter, they give the adjusted p-value, `adjp_h` for
the hand-written converter and `adjp_l` for the LLM-based converter, and
whether the protein was called significant, `sig_h` and `sig_l`. `spiked`
marks the *E. coli* proteins, whose amount changes in every comparison, and
`in_h` and `in_l` say whether each converter's results include the protein. A
protein that MSstats could not test, because one condition has no measurement,
is never called significant, whatever its adjusted p-value.

```{r results}
results <- case$results
head(results, 3)
```

For each comparison, the table below counts the proteins called significant
with each sequence column, and the *E. coli* proteins among them.

```{r counts}
counts <- results[, .(full        = sum(sig_h, na.rm = TRUE),
                      full_spiked = sum(sig_h & spiked, na.rm = TRUE),
                      base        = sum(sig_l, na.rm = TRUE),
                      base_spiked = sum(sig_l & spiked, na.rm = TRUE)),
                  by = .(comparison = Label)]
counts
```

The table below counts, for each comparison, the proteins that both
converters call significant and those that only one of them calls
significant.

```{r overlap}
overlap <- results[, {
  h <- sig_h %in% TRUE
  l <- sig_l %in% TRUE
  .(both = sum(h & l), full_only = sum(h & !l), base_only = sum(!h & l))
}, by = .(comparison = Label)]
overlap
```

Over the `r nrow(overlap)` comparisons, the two converters share
`r sum(overlap$both)` significant calls, while `r sum(overlap$full_only)` are
significant only with the full sequence and `r sum(overlap$base_only)` only
with the base sequence.

# What to check

- Which column the conversion specification reads as `PeptideSequence`. It
  should be the sequence with the modifications, `Full Sequence` in
  MetaMorpheus.
- Do not judge the two columns by the example rows alone, where they are often
  the same. Look for the rows where they differ, for example with
  `tool_output[Base.Sequence != Full.Sequence]` on the full tool output.
- A peptide that the tool output reports with and without a modification must
  stay two features.
